heading: ## Effective expectation reconciliation — round 14
notes: Round-54's T54W2Read15 filed two items on this same heading and routed them to round 55; round 55's fix never landed (the section's bytes at 99c3bc8, 9cf0146, 51d1f0e, 981c5e8b and c0137451 are one and the same, sha 6110606e…, and the section text at base is byte-identical to C0). I re-adjudicate both here rather than carrying them forward unexamined, and neither survives as a false statement. (1) 'before either named round': the only two rounds jointly named in the parenthetical are 18 and 21 (the bash witness-study tool's), so the trailing clause reads 'round 17 came before both rounds 18 and 21', which is TRUE and checkable — `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2a22ade 58e5d53` and `… 2a22ade 370f2df` both succeed, and the commit dates are 2026-10-20 12:06 < 2026-10-20 17:20 < 2026-10-21 09:24. The round-54 reader's stated reason ('names nothing an executor can check') is therefore refuted: the ordering is checkable in one command. What remains is loose wording — 'either' against a parenthesis that names four round numbers (16, 17, 18, 21) — which is a precision/style item, not a false statement, and round 53's own reader (T53W2Read01) had already classified the same phrase as a note with the same reading. Suggest the L1 rewrite it as 'before both rounds 18 and 21' in round 57.

Round-54's T54W2Read15 item 2, 'which the commands below name': likewise not false, but worth a rewording. The parenthetical says the two counts 'belong to .ufo/evidence/round-13/expected.json, which the commands below name: twelve expected checks, thirteen inputs'. The two counts are TRUE (expected.json holds exactly 12 expected_checks and 13 inputs) and the path IS named by what the commands below produce — both round-14 manifests carry `"expected_file": ".ufo/evidence/round-13/expected.json"` and the tool's JSON output prints `"expected_checks": 12` plus a 13-entry `expected_inputs_verified` list — but it is named in the command's OUTPUT and in the manifest's `expected_file` field, not in the command's argv. A reader who greps the two command lines for 'expected.json' finds nothing. Suggested round-57 wording: 'the file each command reads is named in its `expected_file` field and in the tool's JSON output'.

The round attribution in the parenthetical is TRUE but now stale-but-true as an exhaustive list, and a round-57 note should say so. Verified at C0: the three stale pinned inputs are exactly tools/mutate-and-run.sh, tools/bash-witness-study.py and tools/pin-disposition.py (3 of 13), and their first movers after the `git archive 28aeef4` baseline are c699c8c/05a2247 (round 16, the runner), 58e5d53 (round 18) then 370f2df (round 21) (the witness-study tool) and 2a22ade (round 17) (pin-disposition.py) — so 'the runner in round 16, the bash witness-study tool in rounds 18 and 21, and tools/pin-disposition.py in round 17' is accurate as the first-mover chain. It is not a complete list of the rounds in which those three files changed afterwards: the runner also changed in rounds 17, 18, 26, 30, 51 and 54, the witness-study tool in rounds 53 and 54, and pin-disposition.py in rounds 53 and 54, so the live bytes the reader sees at C0 come from those later commits, not from the ones named.

The live-tree exit-2 claim is TRUE but the tool names only the FIRST stale input, so the section's 'three of its thirteen inputs are stale' must be established by hashing the thirteen pins, not by reading the error. Receipt 01/02 show the error naming only tools/bash-witness-study.py; hashing all thirteen inputs independently yields exactly three stale. The section is right to state both facts separately.

The frozen replay reproduces the committed round-14 receipt byte-for-byte except for the `root` field, which is the extracted archive path rather than the lane root: the recorded `unresolved_before` stdout in .ufo/evidence/round-14/verification-final.json and my replay differ in exactly one line (`"root": …`). This is strong evidence that the recipe's replay command is the one that produced the receipt; the tool digest in the replay output (1609a9df…, 'evidence-disposition.py r14') matches the pinned input_sha256 of tools/evidence-disposition.py in verification-final.json, and the archive tree's own tools/evidence-disposition.py is that same r14 build.

The section's claim that the round-14 pin-disposition row is the ONLY repair is TRUE and checkable: diffing the row sets of dispositions-before.json and dispositions.json shows exactly one changed row state (producer_before effective → superseded), and the superseded row keeps raw_receipt (.ufo/evidence/round-13/verification.json), raw_check (producer_before) and superseded_by [producer_before_oracle, producer_after_oracle], both of which are effective and passing in the exit-0 run.

The section's step-3 pointer 'Live-tree form: the round-17 re-pin section (round-18 manifests since then)' resolves and is TRUE: `.ufo/evidence/round-18/dispositions.json` returns 0 clean (effective 11, superseded 1) at the C0 live tree while `.ufo/evidence/round-17/dispositions.json` returns 2 expected_input_digest_mismatch, exactly as the round-17 section itself states.

The step-5 'must not be run again' reasoning is TRUE and mechanically checkable: .ufo/evidence/round-14/capture-context.py has OUTPUT_REL = ".ufo/evidence/round-14/context-receipt.json", i.e. its historical output path is the very path holding the frozen receipt (sha256 05cb55b8…, the same digest the round-15 registry pins), so re-running it would replace the frozen receipt. The maintained retained-only gate the section points at (tools/context-capture.py --check, named in the Round-15 gate/probe registry) exits 0 with id=context_consistent and reports that same receipt digest.

The section's Sources line is accurate at C0: corpus/lessons/round-13-verifier-spotcheck.md exists and its 'Routed defects and residuals' section carries items 1-3 covering exactly this subject matter (the stale expected.json producer_before expectation, the unrecorded injection setup, and the dated knowledge §6); S049 is the Python subprocess environment-mapping source whose teaches cell is the explicit env/child-environment contract; S003 is the StrykerJS incremental source whose Limitations section the knowledge entry re-opens; and corpus/knowledge/incremental-pin-disposition.md §8 is titled 'Empirical correction and backlink — round 14', matching the README's own 'empirical correction8' label for that entry.

Coverage note: this heading's commands were exercised in a `git clone --shared` scratch clone checked out --detach at C0 (git rev-parse --show-toplevel printed the scratch clone path; the clone's `git status --porcelain` returned zero lines after every run), plus an extracted `git archive 28aeef4` tree for the frozen replay. The lane tree was only read (git show / log / cat-file); no lane production file was edited and no mutating git command was run anywhere. Receipts are in .ufo/waves/round-56/w2/T56W2Read02-receipts/ (files 00-15).

Adjacent observation for the L1, outside this heading's scope and therefore not filed as a finding: the fleet census validate command exits 0 and its output is byte-identical to the committed .ufo/evidence/round-56/census-start.stdout, but the census row count does not match this wave's brief. Measured: the census reports 'tameshi rows 142' for the C0 tree, and 'rows 140' for the base registry (the same count a grep of '^| S[0-9]' gives at 981c5e8b), so the round-56 C0 commit c0137451 added TWO SOURCES rows (S281, the in-toto Statement layer specification, and S282, the SLSA provenance specification) — not the one new row the brief assumes, and the resulting count is 142, not 141.
